subject: Scaling Redwood: onboarding 4 additional apps & API key rotation
message_1_subject: Request: onboard four more apps, API key strategy & pricing
message_1_body:
Hi Irene and team,

We are planning to onboard four additional internal apps onto Redwood next quarter (clinical-notes, triage-bot, intake-form, billing-assistant). Current usage for our pilot app is stable but the growth projections mean we need guidance on: 
- whether to issue separate API keys per app or use scoped keys tied to existing keys
- recommended quota and rate limits for each app (we expect varied traffic)
- implications for our renewal — do we amend the reserved capacity, or add pay-as-you-go for the extra capacity?

Approx expected Q3 peak: clinical-notes 250 RPS (short spikes), triage-bot 40 RPS, intake-form 15 RPS, billing-assistant 60 RPS.

Can you point me to a recommended rollout plan and any security/compliance guidance for key rotation? Also attaching a quick spreadsheet with app owners and rough traffic estimates.

Thanks,
Lena Gomez
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health

Attachment: acme_additional_apps_list.xlsx
message_2_subject: Re: Request: onboard four more apps, API key strategy & pricing
message_2_body:
Lena — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Looping in Neha (commercial) and Tessa (solutions) to cover pricing + technical rollout. Quick next steps from our side: 
1) Neha: propose commercial options and delta to current reserved capacity (we'll need peak/95th percentile numbers by app).
2) Tessa: draft a rollout that minimizes risk (canary per app, KV caching guidance, key scoping).
3) I: coordinate timeline and sign-off with your security team for key rotation policy.

Can you confirm if each app must be logically isolated in logs and billing, or if consolidated billing is OK? That affects whether we recommend separate keys per app.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
message_3_subject: Re: Request: onboard four more apps, API key strategy & pricing
message_3_body:
Hi Lena — appreciate the projection numbers. From a commercial perspective we typically offer two paths when customers expand within a renewal window: 

Option A — Reserved capacity amendment: add a modest bump to your committed GPUs / token throughput for the remainder of the term. This gives predictable unit pricing and comes with SLA continuity.

Option B — Hybrid burst: keep current reserved commit, add pay-as-you-go for incremental traffic (useful for spiky apps like clinical-notes).

Ballpark numbers (subject to final telemetry): adding capacity to cover a steady-state increase to ~350 RPS peak across apps would increase monthly committed spend by ~22% vs current. If you prefer, we can model exact costs per app — Irene, can you confirm acceptance criteria for the quote and whether procurement prefers an amendment or a standalone PO?

I will schedule a 30-min call if helpful — proposing Tue 2026-04-13 10:00 AM PT.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Deal: ACME-2026-RNW-42
message_4_subject: Technical plan & key rotation recommendation — clinical-notes canary approach
message_4_body:
Lena — attached is a short technical plan and recommended key rotation steps. High-level recommendations: 

- Keys per app: we recommend issuing one dedicated API key per app (better visibility in logs, per-app quotas, and scoped revocation).
- Rotation: 30-day rotation cadence with staggered overlap (old key active for 48 hours while new key rolls in) to avoid downtime. See attached api_key_rotation_steps.md for scripts and Terraform snippets.
- Rate limits & autoscale: set soft quotas per key with aggressive autoscale triggers for clinical-notes (because of spikes). We'll configure prefix caching for clinical-notes to cut per-token cost.
- Canary rollout: 2% traffic for first 24 hours, 25% for next 48–72 hours, full cutover after stability checks.

Please confirm environment access (staging cluster hostnames and if your SRE wants the TF plan in a PR). Attachments: mca_plan_draft.pdf (draft mutual action plan), api_key_rotation_steps.md.

On Tue, Apr 13, 2026 at 09:15 AM Lena Gomez <lena@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks — can we make rotation scripts idempotent? Our SREs prefer green deploys.

- Tessa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
message_5_subject: Re: Technical plan & key rotation recommendation — clinical-notes canary approach
message_5_body:
Irene / Neha / Tessa — thanks, this looks good. Quick answers: 
- We want separate keys per app and per environment (staging/production).
- Rotation cadence OK — please provide the idempotent scripts (our SRE prefers a 7-day dry-run window).
- Billing: Acme would prefer an amendment to the existing reserved capacity if modeling shows <=25% delta to the current monthly commit. If >25% we will likely procure burst capacity while renegotiating at renewal.

I attached our acceptance criteria and a simple timeline: week 0 prep & key provisioning, week 1 canary (clinical-notes), week 2 triage-bot & intake-form parallel canaries, week 3 full rollout for billing-assistant. Can you confirm if Redwood can provision separate keys + scoped quotas within 48 hours after contract amendment?

Thanks — looping in our onboarding alias.

Lena Gomez
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health
